reading.body:
Kentucky's 2026 session lists 87 bills, but only one, HB455, explicitly addresses artificial intelligence, while separate data center and data privacy bills show the state's attention is on AI's physical and data foundations.

Five bills concern data centers: HB593, HB856, SB319, SB330, and HB544. Their titles give no detail on incentives, siting, or energy, but the cluster indicates the legislature is actively considering the buildings that house AI compute. Four data privacy bills, HB692, HB633, HB559, and HB33, sit alongside narrower measures on rent-setting algorithms, mental health chatbots, automated license plate readers, and name, voice, and likeness rights.

The list records bill introductions and titles only. It does not show whether any measure passed, was amended, or became law, and it does not reveal whether the data center bills address grid capacity, power supply, or energy demand. Kentucky's approach appears piecemeal, but the data cannot confirm outcomes.
